evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: six main arms with thin side arms leaving them at fixed angles and letter glyphs sitting along each arm; by shot-20s the arms are denser and the glyph row is jumbled, so the fixed-lag rule is hard to read.
evidence.ambition: shot-02s: one flat oxblood star on a clay ground with six dot-studded arms and a small mono caption; by shot-20s layered hatching, glyph rows and side arms add layers but no material, lighting or depth.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: clean crisp vector edges and a palette matching the rose-clay and oxblood brief; shot-20s: overlapping glyph smudges and thin hatch lines that alias and shimmer at full size.
evidence.distinctness: shot-08s: six-armed snowflake with letter-born side arms, not a starfield or plasma; a six-armed snowflake is a familiar demo form, but it differs clearly from the Penrose kite tiling of 2026-11-23.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: star is centred but only about 480 px tall, so it does not fill the frame as the brief claims; shot-20s resolves into a full mirrored figure, so start and end are both composed.

pairwise_justification: Penrose 2026-11-23 holds a denser, cleaner development at 20s: ochre and rust kites fill a large triangle. Tonight's 20s is thin hatching over jumbled glyph smudges, so the median wins the head-to-head.

critique.change: Make the glyph row legible at shot-20s: give each arm one clean glyph per lag step, spaced at a constant distance behind the tip, instead of overlapping letters, so the fixed-lag rule reads on screen.
Add material or depth to the arms, such as a ridge shading or a tone step along each main arm, so the shot-02s star stops reading as a flat silhouette.
Remove the mono caption at the bottom-left of shot-02s and show the V*R^2 rule by the tip visibly thinning as its speed rises, so the visuals carry the concept.
